models_evaluated: attention-guided coarse-to-fine multi-task deep learning system (DLS) for knee MRI

links.outcome: Radiologist accuracy and reading time with versus without DLS assistance (randomised comparative study)
links.effect: DLS-assisted junior and senior radiologists had higher accuracy (difference 4.8-8.8% and 4.2-8.2%, all p<0.05) and reduced reading time (by 35.5 and 30.7 s, all p<0.05) vs control.
links.quote: For step 3, the randomised comparative study demonstrated that the junior and senior radiologists in the DLS-assisted group achieved significantly higher accuracy (difference of 4.8-8.8% and 4.2-8.2%, all p < 0.05) and reduced reading time (by 35.5 and 30.7 s, all p < 0.05) compared to the control group for nine knee abnormalities.

links.outcome: DLS accuracy compared with senior radiologists on the same data
links.effect: DLS showed comparable accuracy to senior radiologists for meniscal tear (79.6% vs 78.1%), ACL tear (89.3% vs 89.4%), and MCL injury (87.1% vs 85.7%).
links.quote: For step 1 of validation, the DLS demonstrated comparable accuracy to that of the senior radiologists in classifying meniscal tear (79.6% vs. 78.1%, p = 0.426), ACL tear (89.3% vs. 89.4%, p = 1.000), and MCL injury (87.1% vs. 85.7%, p = 0.565).

links.outcome: DLS AUC on internal versus external test sets
links.effect: AUCs for primary abnormalities fell from 0.898 (internal) to 0.852 and 0.812 (external sets I and II); secondary abnormalities from 0.815 to 0.744 and 0.774.
links.quote: The DLS demonstrated areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.898 (95% confidence intervals [CI], 0.890-0.905) and 0.815 (95% CI, 0.805-0.823), 0.852 (95% CI, 0.830-0.872) and 0.744 (95% CI, 0.721-0.766), and 0.812 (95% CI, 0.771-0.854) and 0.774 (95% CI, 0.733-0.816) for primary and secondary abnormalities on the internal test set, external test set I, and external test set II, respectively.

screen.reason: The study conducts a multi-reader multi-case and randomized comparative reader study evaluating the impact of AI assistance on radiologists' diagnostic performance and reading time.
